data_state.rationale: Index monotonicity is required when method != None. Existing NaN values in cells are never filled by propagation methods — only newly introduced gaps are filled. The shape and dtype of the DataFrame determine what fill_value is compatible.

partitions.monotonic_index: Row index is strictly monotonic increasing or decreasing; e.g., DatetimeIndex(['2010-01-01','2010-01-02','2010-01-03'])
partitions.non_monotonic_index: Row index is not monotonic; e.g., Index(['b','a','c'])
partitions.multiindex_rows: DataFrame has a MultiIndex on rows; e.g., pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples([('a',1),('a',2),('b',1)])
partitions.contains_existing_nan: At least one cell already holds NaN before reindexing; e.g., df with df.iloc[0,0]=np.nan

partitions.labels_with_overlap: New labels partially overlap existing index; missing ones become gaps; e.g., ['Safari','Iceweasel','Chrome']
partitions.labels_no_overlap: None of the new labels exist in the current index; all rows become NaN; e.g., ['X','Y','Z']
partitions.labels_identical: New labels are identical to current index in the same order; no structural change; e.g., df.index.tolist()
partitions.labels_subset: New labels are a strict subset of current index; result has fewer rows; e.g., ['Chrome','Safari']

invalid_cases.desc: Passing both 'labels' and 'index'/'columns' simultaneously raises TypeError; e.g., df.reindex(['a'], index=['b'])

partitions.index_partial_overlap: New row labels partially overlap current; e.g., ['Safari','NewBrowser','Chrome']
partitions.index_no_overlap: New row labels have no match in current index; e.g., ['A','B','C']

invalid_cases.desc: Providing both 'labels' and 'index' raises TypeError; e.g., df.reindex(['a'], index=['b'])

partitions.columns_partial_overlap: New column labels partially overlap current; new columns become NaN; e.g., ['http_status','user_agent']
partitions.columns_no_overlap: No column label matches current; all columns become NaN; e.g., ['X','Y']

invalid_cases.desc: Providing both 'labels' and 'columns' raises TypeError; e.g., df.reindex(['a'], columns=['b'])

partitions.axis_index: Reindex along rows; axis=0 or axis='index'
partitions.axis_columns: Reindex along columns; axis=1 or axis='columns'

invalid_cases.desc: Out-of-range axis raises ValueError; e.g., df.reindex(['a'], axis=2)

partitions.method_none: No propagation; new index labels without a match get NaN; e.g., method=None
partitions.method_ffill: Forward-fill: propagate last valid observation forward to cover gaps; e.g., method='ffill' or method='pad'
partitions.method_bfill: Backward-fill: use next valid observation to fill gap; e.g., method='bfill' or method='backfill'
partitions.method_nearest: Fill with the nearest observation; ties broken by forward preference; e.g., method='nearest'

invalid_cases.desc: method != None on a non-monotonic index raises ValueError; e.g., df with Index(['b','a','c']) and method='ffill'
Unrecognised method string raises ValueError; e.g., method='interpolate'

partitions.fill_default_nan: Default; missing positions filled with NaN; fill_value=np.nan
partitions.fill_numeric: Integer or float replaces NaN for missing positions; e.g., fill_value=0
partitions.fill_string: String replaces NaN for missing positions; e.g., fill_value='missing'

partitions.limit_none: No cap on consecutive fills; limit=None
partitions.limit_positive: Fill at most N consecutive gaps; positions beyond N remain NaN; e.g., limit=1

invalid_cases.desc: Non-positive integer limit raises ValueError; e.g., limit=-1

partitions.tolerance_none: No distance constraint; all in-range fills proceed; tolerance=None
partitions.tolerance_scalar: Single scalar applied to every new label; match only if abs(new - old) <= tolerance; e.g., tolerance=pd.Timedelta('1 day')
partitions.tolerance_list: Per-label list; length must equal len(new_index); e.g., tolerance=[pd.Timedelta('1D'), pd.Timedelta('2D'), pd.Timedelta('1D')]

invalid_cases.desc: List tolerance whose length differs from new index length raises ValueError; e.g., df.reindex(new_idx_len3, tolerance=[1, 2])
tolerance provided without method raises ValueError; e.g., df.reindex(new_idx, tolerance=1) with method=None

partitions.level_none: Standard reindex with no MultiIndex level matching; level=None
partitions.level_specified: Match new index against a single level of a MultiIndex; broadcast result; e.g., level=0 on a (level0, level1) MultiIndex

invalid_cases.desc: level specified on a flat (non-MultiIndex) DataFrame raises TypeError; e.g., df_flat.reindex(new_index, level=0)

partitions.copy_provided: Parameter is accepted but silently ignored in pandas >= 3.0.0; triggers FutureWarning or DeprecationWarning; e.g., copy=True

postconditions.claim: reindex always returns a DataFrame regardless of which parameters are used
postconditions.expected_behavior: isinstance(result, pd.DataFrame) == True

postconditions.claim: when labels (or index) are provided without method, new labels not in the original index produce rows where all cells are NaN
postconditions.expected_behavior: for lbl in set(new_labels) - set(original_index): result.loc[lbl].isna().all() == True

postconditions.claim: labels that exist in both old and new index retain their original values exactly
postconditions.expected_behavior: result.loc[common_labels].equals(original_df.loc[common_labels]) == True

postconditions.claim: when labels (or columns) are provided without method, new column labels not in original columns produce NaN-filled columns
postconditions.expected_behavior: for col in set(new_columns) - set(original_columns): result[col].isna().all() == True

postconditions.claim: the result index equals the new labels passed in, preserving order
postconditions.expected_behavior: list(result.index) == list(new_labels)

postconditions.claim: fill_value replaces NaN for new labels that have no match when method=None
postconditions.expected_behavior: for lbl in set(new_labels) - set(original_index): (result.loc[lbl] == fill_value).all() == True

postconditions.claim: fill_value has no effect on labels that already exist in the original index
postconditions.expected_behavior: result.loc[common_labels].equals(original_df.loc[common_labels]) == True

postconditions.claim: method='ffill' on a monotonic index fills each gap with the last observed value before it
postconditions.expected_behavior: for each new label without direct match: result.loc[lbl] equals the value at the largest original label <= lbl

postconditions.claim: method='bfill' on a monotonic index fills each gap with the first observed value after it
postconditions.expected_behavior: for each new label without direct match: result.loc[lbl] equals the value at the smallest original label >= lbl

postconditions.claim: method='nearest' on a monotonic index fills each gap with the value from the closest original label
postconditions.expected_behavior: for each unmatched new label: result.loc[lbl] equals original value at argmin(abs(original_index - lbl))

postconditions.claim: method != None with a non-monotonic index raises ValueError
postconditions.expected_behavior: raises ValueError

postconditions.claim: existing NaN values in the DataFrame are NOT overwritten by propagation methods
postconditions.expected_behavior: cells that were NaN before reindex remain NaN in result regardless of method

postconditions.claim: limit=N with a fill method caps consecutive fills at N; positions beyond the cap remain NaN
postconditions.expected_behavior: for a run of K consecutive gaps where K > N: only the first N (ffill) or last N (bfill) are filled; the rest are NaN

postconditions.claim: scalar tolerance restricts fills: a gap is filled only when abs(new_label - source_label) <= tolerance
postconditions.expected_behavior: for each new label l: if min distance to original index > tolerance then result.loc[l].isna().all() == True

postconditions.claim: list tolerance applies per-label distance constraints; its length must equal the new index length
postconditions.expected_behavior: len(tolerance) != len(new_index) raises ValueError; otherwise each position i uses tolerance[i] as its distance cap

postconditions.claim: using labels + axis='index' is equivalent to passing index=labels directly
postconditions.expected_behavior: df.reindex(labels, axis='index').equals(df.reindex(index=labels)) == True

postconditions.claim: using labels + axis='columns' is equivalent to passing columns=labels directly
postconditions.expected_behavior: df.reindex(labels, axis='columns').equals(df.reindex(columns=labels)) == True

postconditions.claim: when labels is identical to the current index, the result is equal to the original DataFrame
postconditions.expected_behavior: result.equals(original_df) == True

postconditions.claim: level= on a MultiIndex DataFrame reindexes by matching one level against the new labels, broadcasting across other levels
postconditions.expected_behavior: result.index retains MultiIndex structure; rows whose target level value appears in new_labels are kept; unmatched level values become NaN rows

postconditions.claim: copy parameter (deprecated since 3.0.0) is silently ignored; passing it emits a deprecation warning but does not raise
postconditions.expected_behavior: no exception is raised; result is the same as without copy argument; a DeprecationWarning or FutureWarning is issued
